items.target: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §8 (line 311), the PrefetchWindow.targets sentence
items.text: Current text: '`PrefetchWindow.targets` (implemented): current, +1, −1, +2, −2…; `PrefetchWindowController(client:radius: Int? = nil)` defaults its radius to `configuration.prefetchRadius` (ADR-048) and creates the new handle before releasing the old.' Replacement (draft): after 'current, +1, −1, +2, −2…' insert '; the walk stops at the carousel's farther end (`PrefetchWindow.reach`), so any radius, `Int.max` included, costs what the carousel's size costs (S3-PERF-06)'. Precision: reach = min(max(radius, 0), farther side). The exact wording is therefore 'the walk goes no farther than the radius or the carousel's farther end, whichever is nearer (a negative radius counts as 0)'. Optional addition: `prefetchRadius` and `init(radius:)` stay unclamped by decision. They are in a contract file, and after the clamp any value is safe (S3G-1).

Prefetch.swift:116-120: static func reach(count:current:radius:) -> Int { min(max(radius, 0), max(current, count - 1 - current)) }. Doc comments at :88-89 and :123-124. items.target: docs/DECISIONS.md, ADR-054 (line 456), '*The model's measurement limits (L5-R22 (2)).*'
items.text:
Current text: 'Besides the tolerances of G-17's audit, two rows are **measurement limits of the model, not product promises**: (a) I1 does not owe the registration generation's own `clientStarted`, nor the terminal events of calls (other than the markers) that began after the registration; (b) I2 accepts one extra `clientStarted` in the first gap, the registration engine's own. L5-R13/L5-R19's promise stands … Tightening the model is Stage 3's (Assignments).'

The draft replaces (a) and (b) with two rows: (a′) 'a `subscribe()` stream whose registration engine was unstarted when the call began, and one started while a reopen was parked before its install, are not owed that engine's `clientStarted` and may receive it once'; (a″) 'calls begun while a reopen was parked before its install, and `sync(.force)` calls that returned `.failed` or `.notDue`, are not stamped (they may return without publishing)'. It also records that since Stage 3 the registration generation's `clientStarted` is owed when the registration preceded its start, and so are its stamped calls' terminal events.

Convention: ADR-054 gets an appended 'Amendment (Stage 3 merge, ADR-057)' bullet, as in DECISIONS.md:474-475; the ratified rows are not rewritten.

Evidence to carry: 35 such registrations over the 500 suite seeds (27 created, 8 starting); MT1 and MT2 fail all 10 cases on the tightened model and pass on s3-base's; MC00 is still caught, 10 of 10; 500 seeds run in 2.4 s and 5,000 in 20.2 s at a load of about 30.

Two gaps in the proposed wording, found by reading:
(i) An `events` stream's start order also stays `.unknown` (not owed, one spare accepted) in three cases: its serving engine was unstarted when the action began but had started by its registration turn; the lifecycle wait ended without a registration; or the walk had no oracle tap. (a′) names `subscribe()` streams only.
(ii) A `performMaintenance` call that threw is not stamped, and neither is any call made while the walk had no oracle tap for the serving generation. (a″) names only parked calls and `.failed`/`.notDue` syncs.

items.target: ADR-057's NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW tags
items.source: docs/adr-drafts/s3g.md records none; CLAUDE.md 'Decisions' lists the tagging rule
items.text: The draft records no NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW item. None of s3g's changes touches storage location, on-disk layout, platform floor, dependencies or a public signature. One candidate for the orchestrator to decide: S3G-4's download-before-candidate-check order is an observable behavioural deviation from the prior art, in both `AssetFallbackChain.fetch` and the shim's `CDNAssetResolver.resolveViaNetwork` (R-CAR-2 asks for identical observable behaviour). `fetch('clip', kind: .image)` downloads a whole .mp4 at .userInitiated, stores it, then throws notFound; the confirmer reproduced this 6 of 6 times. K-11/ADR-055 accepts the behaviour. But K-11 is not among ADR-055's NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW items (K-2, K-3, K-5, K-6, K-15), while ADR-037, which covers the facade's other fallback-chain deviations, is tagged NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW.

items.text: S3-B-094, an accepted deviation (S3G-5; L5-R4, L5-R20). Three cases: a call that succeeds on a replaced root that no commit has detected does not reopen until a qualifying failure or a commit; a root check whose own stat fails records nothing; a root that vanishes between withAsset's read of unavailableReason and its lease leases from the vanished store (a read). The cost is one lstat per qualifying failure. Goes to the device plan.

items.source: s3ah.md:239-240 (Proposed document changes 4); S3AH-3 (s3ah.md:118-146); ruling S3AH-3 (S3-B-104, L4-R24(2), ADR-053 assignment)
items.text: Current text (part of line 91): 'Tests use `ManualTimeSource`, and the deterministic suites never sleep for real (R-ENV-1's test of `LiveTimeSource` itself uses only past deadlines and a cancelled one);'. The draft gives the facts but no wording: '`MonotonicInstant.adding(seconds:)` rounds to the nearest nanosecond, and `ManualTimeSource.advance(to:)` lands exactly on its target (L4-R24(2) closed; ADR-053's assignment)'. Suggested replacement (my wording): 'Tests use `ManualTimeSource`, whose `advance(to:)` moves in nanoseconds and lands exactly on its target (awake time moves by the same nanoseconds, saturating; the wall clock moves by the gap in seconds; an earlier target moves nothing; L4-R24(2), closed in Stage 3, ADR-057), and the deterministic suites never sleep for real (R-ENV-1's test of `LiveTimeSource` itself uses only past deadlines and a cancelled one); `MonotonicInstant.adding(seconds:)` rounds to the nearest nanosecond instead of truncating, so `a.adding(seconds: b.seconds(since: a)) == b` for every gap below 2^50 ns (about 13 days), and production deadlines move by at most half a nanosecond, without the old low bias (ADR-057);'
items.code_check: TRUE at 8d86acb. Time.swift:33 is `let delta = (seconds * 1_000_000_000).rounded()`, which uses Swift's default rule (to nearest, ties away from zero). The NaN/zero/negative guard at :27-29 and the saturation at :35-39 are unchanged. At s3-base the line was `let delta = seconds * 1_000_000_000`, truncated by `UInt64(delta)`. ManualTimeSource.swift:148-160: :150 computes the gap in ns, :151 moves the wall clock by `deadline.seconds(since:)`, :152 sets monotonic to old + gap, :153-154 move the awake clock with saturating `addingReportingOverflow`, and :155 calls `collectDue`. At s3-base this function called `advance(by:)` through `seconds(since:)`. Tests: ModelBehaviourTests.swift:169-185 (20,005 gaps, seed 0x5EED_0000_0104, expects 0 shortfalls); ManualTimeSourceTests.swift:65-98 (2,004 gaps up to 2^60 ns, with a sleeper at the target for the first 64); :101 (an earlier target is a no-op). Merged-head --full on e840b0e (identical files): the advance(to:) test passed in 4.459, 4.315 and 4.559 s (debug) and 13.651 s (TSan).

items.text: A-4.7 says '`..foo`, `...`, `.` and `%41` stay allowed'. That no longer holds for `.`. An empty or `.` (also `%2E`, `%2e`) `/`-separated segment, and any backslash, are now `RemotePathViolation.parentSegment` (S3AH-1). They are counted after the leading slashes that `absolute` and `authority` already report: `/abs` stays [absolute]; `//cdn.example/x` stays [authority, absolute]; `https://evil/x` stays [scheme, authority]; `///x` is [authority, absolute, parentSegment]; `https:///x` is [scheme, authority, parentSegment]; `a/?x` is [parentSegment, queryOrFragment]. `%2F` and `%5C` stay literal to the new rule (`a/%2E%2Fb` and `a/%5Cb` are accepted, as the transport accepts them), while the `..` check still treats them as separators (A-4.7, stricter by design). `..foo`, `...` and `%41` stay allowed. Also record: two pre-existing WP-A tests became stricter. In `R-MAN-2: remotePath must be relative, without parent segments, scheme, authority, control characters, query or fragment`, `a/./b` moved to the rejected list. In `R-MAN-2: rules and identifier hashing see the same bytes in bridged and native strings`, the expected list gained `.remotePathInvalid(.parentSegment)`. Neither is a CDN test, so MIGRATION.md (G3) does not apply. Cost: one table load per ordinary byte and at most three byte compares at a `/`. items.text: The prior art fetched paths such as `a//b.png` through `appendingPathComponent`. Since D-6 the transport has refused such paths on every fetch (`failed(.nextRun)`, waiters answered `.serverUnavailable`). Since S3AH-1 the decoder quarantines them with a diagnostic. So a published manifest that relies on an empty or `.` segment, a trailing slash or a backslash does not behave as it did with the prior art (R-MAN-1). No valid shipped fixture has such a path. This is owner information, not a NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW tag, unless the orchestrator decides otherwise.

items.text: Line 836 now reads: "Accepted: a P-13 \"batch\" is one deletion unit: at most 64 unlinks and at most `BlobDeletionUnit.budget` (B-10); P-13 asserts the maximum unit duration (ADR-050; the owner rules on the proposal there); deletable keys are kept in an ordered set so selection is O(batch)." Suggested wording: "each reap run lists the deletable keys once (filter and sort) and reads them through a cursor, so a run is linear in the keys after that sort".

items.target: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §10.1 R13 (line 403), text amendment (not a new row)
items.text: Draft: "R13's text changes as above (a rescued counted doom no longer counts)". Current R13: "... every byte an eviction, an `apply`'s plan, a purge, a quarantine, a recorded failure or a record's last integrity failure releases afterwards (this run's included) counts toward the need, re-checked before each candidate, so a run that awaited while another released bytes frees only what is still needed (C-2)". Replacement: "... every byte an eviction, an `apply`'s plan, a purge, a quarantine, a recorded failure, a record's last integrity failure, or `apply`'s and `admit`'s own releases (prune, a replaced detached record's or an adopted record's previous blob) releases afterwards (this run's included) counts toward the need, re-checked before each candidate. A count by `apply` or `admit` is taken back when that doom is rescued (adoption, `setResidency`, a binding, a publication's dedupe), so `releasedBytes` can fall, and it is counted again when a rescuing publication binds nothing and dooms the key afresh (S3B-9). Counts made by eviction, purge or quarantine are not taken back (CCR for WP-C). A run that awaited frees only what is still needed (C-2)." No await was added. Readers take differences against the value they read at their measurement, so a lower value makes a run free more, never less (s3b.md:328-329).

items.text:
ADR-052:
(a) OI-14 (a residual at L391 and L399, a candidate at L401) is resolved by S3B-9 for apply and admit. A new residual remains: dooms WP-C counted are not taken back (CCR for WP-C).
(b) OI-12 (a candidate at L401) is recorded by S3B-10, with a CCR for WP-C.
(c) Stage 3 assignment (1), C-22/OI-9: the reap queue's re-insertion is now a cursor (S3B-5). The chunked grace start was not done (S3B-14; it lies beyond the reference scale). "Releasing a unit's closure before the actor resumes" was not addressed in s3b.
(d) Assignment (3), OI-15 ("narrow R3, add probe ZP7-OI1b as a test"), is superseded by S3B-11: R3 stands, with a CCR for WP-F. L390's "R3 stays literal for Level 3" now holds through Stage 3.
(e) Assignment (5), P-13, was ruled by the owner (ADR-050 amendment).
(f) "Any change to WP-B's grace start or doom rules revisits orphan GC's reap window (C-23)": s3b changed neither, and reapWindowClosed is independent of the reaper queue, so no revisit is needed.
ADR-053:
- §12.5 T2-06's cross-launch collision case is now written (S3B-8).
- L4-R24(6) is answered: release builds do not copy the blob table (S3-B-016: 0.103 ms for 1,000 gains at 100,000 blobs).
- The routed item on WP-B's FreeSpace.pendingReclaim is answered by S3-B-015: not reproduced, and only the documented states apply.
- L4-R24(5), the late joiner with OI-15, stays with S3B-11's CCR.
ADR-022's amendment (through ADR-053, L140: "reported to WP-B, Stage 3") is answered by S3-B-015. The engine's fresh read stays.
ADR-020's amendment (L129, "Accepted residue for Stage 3 with OI-15"): the residue remains, now with a CCR for WP-F.
ADR-050: B-10's deletion-unit bounds are unchanged, but the queue's carry is now a cursor (S3B-5). For P-13, S3B-12's options are superseded by the owner's amendment (2026-10-29, option A, p99).
ADR-046: "WP-B calls WP-C only through two opt-in hooks" gains an exception: WP-B writes WP-C's contract field releasedBytes (S3B-9).

items.source: docs/adr-drafts/s3b.md:160-169 ("The 1.5 bound is the benchmark's own (SPEC §6 has none for the reaper)"); ruling S3B-5 ("record the release measurement at 10k/20k/40k")
items.text: S3B-5 asked only that the release measurement be recorded. The reapScaling benchmark adds two --perf assertions that no SPEC §6 budget backs. First, the 40k/20k ratio is judged against P-4's `doubling_ratio_max` (2.5, read through QualityBudgets). Second, it asserts seconds[40,000] <= 1.5 x control[40,000], where 1.5 is a literal of the benchmark's own. It also takes the best of three runs per size, interleaved with a 20-key-batch control. ADR-057 should record both bounds as local to the benchmark (a borrowed P-4 ratio and a literal control bound), and that the deterministic test reaperWorkListIsLinear carries the guarantee.

items.target: docs/DECISIONS.md ADR-057: three change requests for the orchestrator's ruling
items.text:
(1) S3B-11, for WP-F. This is a package signature, so it needs the orchestrator's ruling under S3-R6. Draft, verbatim: "before transferring a record that is `absent(.evicted)` (or a shared-content late joiner) whose expected key is live, the engine calls a new WP-B package primitive `bindToLiveContent(_ id:) async throws -> AssetLocation?` that binds by `adoptKnownBlob`'s rule restricted to a **live** key (referenced; never doomed, purged or corrupt, so no eviction is undone), commits with the coalesced window, publishes at the caller's urgency and returns the location; WP-B adds it with an exhaustive test over the blob states (`live`, `doomed(unreferenced|purged|corrupt)`, `deleting`, absent, publishing)." Probes: ZP7-OI1b, ZP8-OI15.
(2) S3B-10, for WP-C (other-wp:c). Draft, verbatim: "WP-B would add `StoreCoreState.reapedSince` (a ring of the last N reaped keys with a serial) and an internal `doomOrphans(_:learntBefore:)` that skips a key reaped after the serial; WP-C would use it in place of the per-run window. Liveness only; each occurrence is logged (`.info`)."
(3) S3B-9 cycle 2, for WP-C. Draft, verbatim: "WP-C's counting sites (`QuotaEviction.swift` `evict`, `StorePurge.swift`, `IntegrityBookkeeping.swift`) could count through WP-B's `countRelease(of:bytes:)` instead of adding to `releasedBytes` directly, so that a rescue of their dooms is taken back too (and `acquireReference`'s `.replaced` would then take back a counted `purged`/`corrupt` doom)." This is still open at the merged head, including any counting sites the s3c merge added.

items.target: docs/RESIDUAL-RISKS.md / ADR-057: P-13 per-unit wall time
items.text:
Cause (S3B-12): one `unlink(2)` stalls in the kernel about once every 850–1,060 unlinks with 256-way fan-out, and every 490–550 in a flat directory. The stalls recur by count, not on a timer, and do not depend on anything the store controls.
Hunter, at load 12.9: 7–13 stalls over 2 ms per 10,000 unlinks, maximum 4.4–6.6 ms. Under load 30–90, unlinks over 4 ms per 10,000 were 18 at default QoS, 136 at utility, 333 at background and 4 at user-interactive.
Confirmer, at load 93–106: stall periodicity in a flat directory 532, 1,075, 2,138, 2,655, 3,183, 3,693; with fan-out and `.noindex` 1,054, 2,091, 3,149, 4,281, 5,600. At utility QoS, 322–342 stalls against 135–155 for the spin control.
The draft's run (release, d66eb2f, load 8.9 -> 5.7): 0.598 s in 562 units. Unit maximum 7.869 ms (p50 0.962, p95 0.993); on-CPU maximum 1.003 ms. Four units over 5 ms; seven unlinks over 4 ms, maximum 7.688 ms. The total, 0.60 s against 2.0 s, passes.
Classification: the owner's ruling (option A, nearest-rank p99; batch_ms_max stays 5 ms), with S3B-12 as its evidence. P-13 sits inside the accepted --full FAIL.
Orchestrator figures on e840b0e (not from the draft): three quiet runs at load 4.14 -> 3.65 passed with p99 4.89, 4.81 and 4.31 ms (maxima 10.51, 9.70 and 8.00 ms). P-13's independent verifier (wf_19408ffa-9ba) found that every run on e840b0e had exactly the 5 units over 5 ms that a nearest-rank p99 tolerates at n 509–528. It estimates that about 30% of runs fail the p99 (17 of 53, Wilson 95% interval 0.21–0.45), some at a quiet load.

items.target: docs/RESIDUAL-RISKS.md / ADR-057: the kill-then-power-loss crash test's hang guard at extreme load
items.text:
Test: `R-STO-5: a process kill followed by a power loss in the next lifetime preserves I-1…I-5`. S3B-7 memoized its reopen per distinct surviving disk: 470–509 pairs per case, with 43–55 distinct disks under powerLossDropUnsynced and 191–218 under powerLossKeepMetadata. No pair, point, mode, slice or assertion was cut.
TSan, the test alone: the old version took 18.202 s (load 14.1 -> 11.7) and 11.138 s (9.7 -> 7.9); the memoized version 6.295 s (11.1 -> 9.7) and 9.178 s (7.9 -> 8.9). Inside full TSan storage runs: 22.039 s (load about 15) and 23.049 s (12.6 -> 8.1). The verifier, the test alone at load 137 -> 280: 21.201 s.
Inside the verifier's full TSan storage run at load 277 -> 628 (976.278 s in all), all 8 cases overran one minute, with 62 follow-on `.cancelled` issues. The backlog's overruns were at loads 441–834.
Classification: S3-R4. The condition for raising the guard (over half the limit under TSan at load about 30) is not met, so it stays at .minutes(1).

This covers quota eviction (reason unreferenced), purge and quarantine, and a purged or corrupt doom that a verified publication replaces. items.target: docs/RESIDUAL-RISKS.md / ADR-057: S3-B-015, pendingReclaim with no deadline
items.text: Not reproduced. A probe, not committed, made the commit of an apply that prunes a 300-byte blob fail four ways: EIO on the index.tmp rename, ENOSPC on its write, EIO on the root sync and EIO on the file sync. apply threw, pendingReclaim was 300, and the key was blocked on acknowledgement and then on commit, but `nextDeadline()` was never nil. The test configuration's zero commitMinimumInterval makes the retry delay zero; the facade's default of 0.25 s doubles up to 5 minutes. A doomed key counts in pendingReclaim with no deadline only in the documented states: unavailable (B-15), degraded (store-1 S1-11), leased, and acknowledgement-blocked after an unacknowledged install (store-1 S1-13). F-25's single sighting fits the last. Classification: S3B-14. The engine's fresh read stays.

items.target: docs/RESIDUAL-RISKS.md / ADR-057: the reapScaling benchmark under load
items.text:
The 40k/20k ratio alone is noise-prone under load: one run of the old reaper passed at 1.996, so the benchmark now takes the best of three and also judges each run against an interleaved control. Times at 10,000 / 20,000 / 40,000:
- before (s3-base, a single run), load 27.9 -> 42.1: 0.911 / 2.033 / 2.966 s; controls 0.426 / 0.875 s.
- after (1daf8bc), load 13.5 -> 12.0: 0.166 / 0.333 / 0.653 s; ratio 1.96; controls 0.310 / 0.633 s.
- final (d66eb2f), load 8.9 -> 5.7: 0.161 / 0.324 / 0.648 s; ratio 2.00; controls 0.323 / 0.651 s.
- gates run (a5edd1e), load 49 -> 8.7: 0.162 / 0.327 / 0.655 s; ratio 2.007 against 2.5; controls 0.313 / 0.632 s; 40,000 against its control 1.036 against 1.5.
- s3-base's reaper spliced in: 0.244 / 0.658 / 1.985 s; ratio 3.018 and against-control 3.131, both failing.
The verifier measured the old reaper at 2.47 and 3.29 times its control, and the fixed one at 0.98–1.04 times. Classification: S3-R5, since a miss caused only by load is not blocking. The deterministic test reaperWorkListIsLinear carries the guarantee.

S3B-12's unlink-stall periodicity was measured on host APFS; device behaviour is unverified (S3-B-021). It belongs in DEVICE-TEST-PLAN, not as a verified API row. conflicts_with_rulings: S3B-12 against the owner's later P-13 ruling (ADR-050 amendment of 2026-10-29; s3-rulings-s3b.md S3B-12, 'P-13 stays the owner's'). The draft was written before the ruling and treats P-13 as open. It offers three options: (B) batch_ms_max of about 15 ms, (A) a percentile, calling p98 'robust', and (C) judging actor holds instead (s3b.md:375-382). It reports `BenchStorage.swift:249:13 … longest <= batchBudget` as the known owner item (s3b.md:383-388, :546-548), and asks DECISIONS to record 'S3B-12's options for the owner's P-13 decision' (s3b.md:520-521). The owner chose option A at the nearest-rank p99, not p98, and batch_ms_max stays 5 ms. The merged head asserts `p99 <= batchBudget` (BenchStorage.swift:243 and :253; d97e4e7). The ruling wins. ADR-057 records S3B-12 as the evidence behind the ruling, marks the options and the 'longest <= batchBudget' failure as superseded, and keeps S3B-12's p98 view as information only (orchestrator follow-up P3 and P8).

S3-R4 ('record each [raised hang guard] with the measured durations and load'). The reapScaling benchmark has carried `.timeLimit(.minutes(3))` since its first commit (BenchStorage.swift:270; 8b3fc89). The draft records no measured duration or reason for it; its only figure is the whole 7-benchmark StorageBenchmarks run, 31.091 s in release (s3b.md:546). Benchmarks in other WPs carry guards of .minutes(3) to .minutes(20) (BenchSync, BenchCleanup, BenchSyncCycle21 and 22). The orchestrator should either record this raise in ADR-057 with a measurement, or rule that S3-R4, which is about TSan durations, does not apply to release-only benchmarks.

S3-R6 ('Contract files may change only where this file authorises it, bodies only'). StoreCoreState.swift is a contract file (ARCHITECTURE §1 row 16). It gained three stored properties, `countedReleases`, `provisionallyRescued` and `lastReap` (StoreCoreState.swift:175-187, +13 lines). These are declarations, not bodies. s3-rulings-s3b.md authorises no contract-file change, and the draft's 'Authorised edits outside WP-B' leaves this out (s3b.md:469-477). The properties are internal and in memory only, with no public or package signature, and §1.1 lets WP-B add fields to its own sub-struct. ADR-057 needs to ratify the change explicitly.

Scope of S3B-9's authorisation ('count a pruning apply's releases in WP-B's release path'). The fix goes beyond pruning. Cycle 1 also counts admit's releases and the previous blob of a replaced detached record or an adopted record. Cycle 2 lowers WP-C's contract field `releasedBytes` when a counted doom is rescued (AssetStore+References.swift:109), which contradicts that field's contract doc, 'never decreases' (EvictionState.swift:20-21). The draft files all of this under S3B-9's authorisation (s3b.md:326-329 and :471-474), though the ruling names pruning releases only and was not re-issued for cycle 2. No WP-C file changed, and readers take differences, so a lower value frees more, never less. Even so, the wider scope and the non-monotonic contract field need explicit ratification in ADR-057.

items.target: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §4.6 quota eviction (line 153)
items.text: Current: '…candidates are computed off the actor and marked in chunks of whole blobs, each ending at the first blob boundary at or past `EvictionState.chunk` (1,000) records with a no-op metadata unit between, each re-validated against its holders read with at most one scan of the records per turn;'. Add the draft's text: 'a blob of more records than a chunk is a chunk of its own, taken a chunk of records per turn; its first turn checks every record, a later turn that the records left are exactly the blob's holders (each still holds it and the reference count matches) and its own records, and a failed check stops the blob, the records already taken staying evicted on the live blob (Stage 3 ruling S3C-2)'. Three precisions for the writer. (a) The parenthesis leaves out the fallback: when the count differs, the turn's one scan must find no holder beyond the records left (a publication's provisional reference passes, a bound id does not). (b) The earlier clause on the same line, 'candidates are blobs, evicted with all their records', needs a qualifier: for a blob of more records than a chunk, only while no check between its turns fails (Decision S3C-2, which amends C-1). (c) A started blob is finished, or stopped by a failed check, whatever other releases did meanwhile: the need is checked only before each candidate. items.target: docs/DECISIONS.md ADR-057: ratify Decision S3C-2; it amends C-1, recorded by reference in ADR-052 (line 393)
items.text:
The draft asks the orchestrator to ratify Decision S3C-2.
- Options: (a) stop on a failed check between turns, keeping the records already taken; (b) roll them back; (c) one turn (the R8 exception).
- Decision: (a). Nothing is released; the blob stays live with the remaining records (the state C-3's `stillReferenced` already produces); the next run takes the rest.
- Scope: only blobs of more records than a chunk (1,000), and only when a change happens between their turns; a change before the first turn keeps the blob whole.
- A started blob is finished even if other releases met the need meanwhile.
- Consequence: a split blob's records are downloaded again on demand and dedupe onto the live blob.
ADR-052:393 records C-1 as 'eviction candidates are blobs, evicted with all their records'; add the exception.

items.text:
WP F:
- R-SYN-13, three tests in EngineFirstReadingTests.swift:
  - `R-SYN-13: an asset that failed offline before the engine's first conditions reading is retried once that reading shows a satisfied path`
  - `R-SYN-13: an offline failure that arrives after the engine's first conditions reading showed a satisfied path is retried at once`
  - `R-SYN-13: an unsatisfied first conditions reading retries nothing and the satisfied reading after it retries the asset once`
- R-SYN-6 (EngineRunIntegrityCapTests.swift): `R-SYN-6: a run over an asset failed at the integrity cap ends completeWithFailures with an integrity failure for it`

- R-SYN-2 (EngineFollowTests.swift):
  - `R-SYN-2: an apply moves only the jobs of the ids it changed and leaves every other waiting job as it was`
  - `R-SYN-2: an apply that moves more jobs than one turn takes follows them a bounded slice per turn with every invariant holding between turns`
  - `R-SYN-2: a job held for a manifest catch-up stays held until the follow that may move it has ended`
- R-SYN-12 (EngineEventOrderTests.swift):
  - `R-SYN-12: a lagging subscriber receives a run's syncStarted before that run's syncProgress`
  - `R-SYN-12: a subscriber stalled across two runs receives the second run's syncStarted before its syncProgress`

items.text: PROBE-C17-ADMIT-DURING-APPLY (RR-17, seed 1_618_202) gives a wrong `notFound` under a race. The ruling says to mark it for the owner in Stage 5's RESIDUAL-RISKS. The race: an admission lands while an older apply that omits the id is in flight, and that apply's follow answers the waiter `notFound` although the store lists the id. Two options, neither taken: (a) defer the decision to the catch-up's follow; (b) record the ids joined unlisted.

items.target: docs/RESIDUAL-RISKS.md and ADR-057: the ENOSPC class, a known residual correctness risk
items.source: s3f.md:8520-8629; S3-R28 item 1c (rulings:1582-1665); close ruling point 4 (rulings:1750-1765)
items.text:
By owner ruling, the whole class is exempt: an answer that differs between the two visit orders, caused by an event inside an ENOSPC window. The window runs from a transfer's or a publication's ENOSPC end to the return of `spaceFailed`'s free-space read.
- Correct #1, PROBE-C22C-TS-DRAIN-JOIN, seed 2_029_101: visited first, the callers get `failed(insufficientSpace(required: 100000, available: 31318659))` and T starts once; swept first, `ok(100000 B)` ×3 and two starts. The control, seed 2_029_201, gives `ok` and two starts in both orders.
- Correct #2, PROBE-C22C-APPLY-IN-READ, seed 2_029_301: visited first, `failed(insufficientSpace(…, available: 31318658))` and one start; swept first, `ok(100000 B)` ×2 and two starts.
- Both still reproduce on d88bdb1 (c23 #8).
- Limits of the probes: both cap `maxAttemptsPerRun` at 1 (the default is 2) and script the second attempt to succeed.
- Suspected but UNCONFIRMED: W-AWAY, W-DB, W-JOIN-HOP (at a publication's end, and in the late drain), the former step-0 shapes, and f1c-review §6's shapes.
- What would close it: route Q, 44-67 h, after a 3-5 h independent check.
- The owner's re-open criterion: field frequency.
- Still blocking inside the window: a broken MUST or invariant, a hang, or a flaky test; each goes to the owner. A late-drain difference outside the window: the orchestrator asks the owner in one line.
items.code_check: The window is at EngineFailures.swift:196-212, EngineDispatch.swift:1259 and :1298-1301, and EngineFailures.swift:564-596. Frozen by item 1c: `metInItsAttempt` at EngineJobs.swift:289-297, `relane`'s guard at :327, T20 at :360-364. All present at HEAD.

items.target: docs/RESIDUAL-RISKS.md and ADR-057: N25's three (known misses by S3-R28 item 3)
items.text:
All three are estimates after route C and item 3b's merge, brought up to f3c's review:
1. Failed user jobs with `.retry` deadlines under one to three prefetch groups: about 500 ms if the origin admits a user request, derived from (571.12 − 36.24) ms / 10,000 ≈ 53 µs per heap scan; 9-18 ms otherwise. The refused form is 11.9-22.5 ms. Production adds 15-60 ms from `originID`. What would close it: A-6 brings it to 11.5-18 ms, an in-place re-admission to 7-12 ms; f3c's route core is 12-18.5 h on top of route C and 3b.
2. A bulk waiter under three prefetch groups: 12.9-23.3 ms.
3. A prefetch group and a bulk group under a third group's pending claim: about 21-34 ms.
The swept-first backoff is RR-25.

items.target: docs/DECISIONS.md ADR-057 (new): S3D-1 record
items.text:
Record S3D-1 as fixed.
(1) Newest-request serial. It is taken after the entry token check and before the first await, checked after the listing, and cleared by the newest request and on `.finished`. Serials are unique for the coordinator's life.
(2) FIFO delivery. Each attach gets one unbounded control stream, drained by one control task that the handle's init starts. The task captures the stream and the coordinator, never the handle. `Waiter.end(with:)` and the handle's `deinit` finish the stream.
(3) Cycle 2's rewrite loop after each write. The single-writer variant (one write in flight per name, with a second table) was rejected: a request would return before its value reached the OS task, so the handle's next control (a pause) could reach the driver first. The loop is bounded by the requests made, and `.finished` ends it.
(4) The two `priorityRequests` clears are equivalent mutants.
(5) MG. The FIFO test checks MG's first effect, its listing, on the fake driver's ordered `calls` log (defc67e). The draft calls the test 'not fully deterministic, by nature'.
(6) Test seams: `FakeBackgroundSessionDriver.holdNextPriority()` and `releasePriority()` (signal 'priority held'), `priorityChanges` in landing order, and `calls`. `BackgroundInterleavingTests` now uses `@testable import ZTronAssetTransport` to await `controlTask`.
Commits: b287a88, e7b9377, 0269a1a, c1395d3, a51f37f, 2528a8c, defc67e, 95bb342.

items.target: docs/DECISIONS.md ADR-057 (new): S3D-2 record
items.text: Record S3D-2 as fixed: failing tests in 1e3bee2, fix in fdf5a3d; `AssetClient` is untouched. The relay keeps every handler, oldest first, and never stores an empty list. `accept` appends; `complete(identifier:)` calls and removes the oldest handler still waiting. Why the oldest: the facade follows each `accept` with one `complete`, issued after a wait that began after that handler was accepted. By the k-th `complete`, k such waits have returned, and at least one of them began after the k-th handler was accepted, so the k-th handler's events were staged. Options not taken: calling every waiting handler at each `complete`, which would call a later handler before its own wait returned; and a ticket per handler, which would change `AssetClient` (WP-G). On s3-base, one completion called only the second handler, and the first was never called.

S3D-4: S2-19 was written (c69327e) against the loopback server and the real URLSession backend. Four transfers end staged, failed (404), paused without a validator, and cancelled. For each, a reader that holds only the update stream returns exactly [terminal]. Afterwards the four `transfer` intervals have ended, `liveTransfers()` is empty, no unfinished URLSession task remains, and weak references to the four handles are nil. The test is not vacuous: a scratch control reader in `DataTransferHandle.init` makes it fail. Cycle 3 (22d1e78) moved the interval check after `await rig.stop()`. `stop()` returns after `didBecomeInvalidWithError`, which the serial delegate queue delivers after every completion, its `finish()` and that `onTermination`.

items.source: docs/adr-drafts/s3d.md:408 (S3-B-052); ruling S3D-6 ('NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW items stay as ratified')
items.text:
D-10 stays NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW as ratified: an explicit `shutdown()` cancels in-flight background downloads (the drop-to-cancel rule).

Add cycle 3's nuance to the owner's question: the cancel is best-effort.
- With FIFO delivery, the engine's `handle.cancel()` waits behind any pending control of that handle.
- If a priority change is still listing, the cancel arrives after `remote.invalidate()`. That call uses `finishTasksAndInvalidate()`, so the OS task goes on and the cancel reaches nothing.
- Probe on the cycle-3 tree, run in a scratch copy: `PROBE shutdownCancelQueuedBehindPriority cancellations=[] priorityChanges=[]`.

The draft calls this 'Not a MUST, and not new in kind'. Before Stage 3, each control's own Task raced `invalidate()` too, and `consumerGone` stays an independent path.

If the owner keeps D-10 as a guarantee, there are two options:
- `invalidate()` cancels the live names' OS tasks before it releases the session;
- a `.cancel` control supersedes pending `.priority` controls.
Neither was taken, because each changes the recorded behaviour of D-10 or of S3-CONC-01.

Classified by S3D-6, and by S3-R8 (pre-existing in kind).

items.target: ADR-057; DECISIONS ADR-052 OI-10 (stays open for WP-F); route as other-wp:f
items.text: The OI-10 class remains outside Transport. WP-F's `EngineLiveTransportTests` uses loopback rigs with `requestTimeout: 10` and responses that stall until the test acts (releasing a group, preempting, shutting down). A host that delays that action by more than 10 s turns the stall into `transient(.timedOut)`. Figures: in OI-10, 191 of 500 transfers timed out at load 110–327 (c.md:1167-1170); S3-B-055's two tests failed at load up to 468.9 (ADR-053 :436). Classified by S3-R8: other-wp:f, non-blocking, routed by the orchestrator. Within Transport, by design, the three kept-short tests (10 s) and `connectionReuse` (50 s) can still time out under extreme load. That would be a false failure, never a false pass: for the three, a firing timeout is what they detect; for `connectionReuse`, the timeout runs on a queued request's wall clock.

items.text: The oldest-first argument assumes that each `complete` follows a wait that began after its handler was accepted and returned only once that wake's events were staged. But `awaitBackgroundEvents()` returns at once when a finish arrived before anybody waited (`unclaimedFinishes`). A buffered earlier finish therefore satisfies the next wait without a new wake. S3D-2 inherits this rather than introducing it, and L5-R5 calls it 'a race WP-D tolerates'. Classified by S3-R8 (pre-existing behaviour that a recorded ruling accepts; ADR-054). The trigger is device-only.

items.text: Known miss in cycle 1. The draft recorded that two writes for one name are in flight together only when the callers overlap their calls, and that no production caller does. That premise was wrong. Each attach has its own control task. A start can join the task and replace the first attach while that attach's write is in flight; the joining handle's write can then land first. The OS task stays at the older priority while `liveTransfers()` reports the newer one. items.target: Test-writing guidance for Stages 4-5 (SPEC 7.2 practice; ADR-057)
items.text: `Task.value` ignores cancellation. A test that awaits a task should join it through a handler that cancels the task when the test is cancelled (`withTaskCancellationHandler`, as in `controlsDelivered`). Otherwise a hang past `.timeLimit` holds the whole run. In cycle 1 that run had to be stopped by hand at 9 min; with the cancelling join, the same mutant run ended on its own in 130 s, the rebuild included.

items.target: docs/DECISIONS.md, ADR-057: S1, the long-purge log line, a soft contract (close point 5)
items.text:
Carry the draft's decision into DECISIONS.md. The ruling requires it: 'ADR-057 carries it into docs/DECISIONS.md at the merge'.

Context: the owner's re-open criterion for the known misses is how often they happen in the field, and nothing in the kit measured that.

Options (s3f.md:8216-8229):
- S1: a log line.
- S2: a MetricsSnapshot field.
- S3: a diagnosticReport() key.
- S4: a signpost interval.
- N0: nothing.
S2 to S4 each change the public API (NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW).

Decision: S1, by ruling. What it does:
- In performPurge's first turn, it reads the injected clock right after `commitTurnMarksForTests?(false)`, with the job and group counts as the turn begins (O(1)).
- After `?(true)` it reads the clock again.
- When the turn is strictly longer than SyncEngine.turnTimeLimit (0.010 s), it writes one .info line on .sync: `long purge turn: <ms> ms, <jobs> jobs, <groups> groups`, with the milliseconds to two decimals.
- The line holds no id, hash, URL, path or key.
- It adds no await and no spawn, so no REENTRANCY row, and changes no public API.

Consequences:
- The text, category, level and threshold are a soft contract. An app counts long purge turns through its own LogSink or OSLogStore.
- OSLogSink logs with privacy .public and maps .info to OSLogType.info. Whether OSLogStore keeps .info lines is UNVERIFIED (C7).
- The measured interval is the benches' first-turn interval (the seam marks). It excludes the formatting of the line itself and the join registration after it.
- Tests: two R-OBS-1 tests (e7cf01a red first, green from f38dd8c).
- Open survivor: s1-late-start (c23 #4).
- NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW applies only if S2 to S4 are chosen later.

The ruling estimated 1.5-3 h for S1.

DECISIONS.md:349 gives option A's premise as 'measured p99 ≈ 1 ms'. The p99 is now 4.3-4.9 ms, inside the APFS stall tail. p95 is about 0.99 ms, and the unit's on-CPU maximum is about 1.0 ms.

DECISIONS.md:368 is wrong in three places:
- 'Every quiet run had 2-4 units over 5 ms out of 490-562'. The four runs on e840b0e had 5, 5, 5 and 5, and the cycle-20 run at a load of 3.6 had 7.
- 'A run passes with up to five stalled units'. That holds only for 500 ≤ n ≤ 599. The nearest-rank p99 tolerates 4 for n < 500, 5 for 500-599 and 6 for n ≥ 600.
- It expects failures only under 'heavy load'. Failures at a quiet load exist:
  - .build-orch/l3-bench.log:116: 8 of 494 over, at loads 1.95-2.56;
  - s3f-probes-c20 bench.log:141: 7 of 494, at 2.3-3.7;
  - c19 bench.log:140: 9 of 507, at 5.24;
  - c22 bench.log:141: 5 of 478 against a tolerance of 4, at 2.6-5.6.

ADR-050 also omits S3B-12's rating, '(A, marginal) ... p98 would be robust' (docs/adr-drafts/s3b.md:378, :381-382).

The owner's exact words (29 Oct, 14:25 UTC): 'Do not set any budget stop. List P99'. The orchestrator read them as option A and told the owner at 14:30 UTC. No correction was found.

Mark the amendment 'not independently verified' until its verifier checks it.

items.text:
Known misses by the owner's ruling N25 (S3-R28 item 3). The owner's words: 'leave these three cases out of cycle 23 and record them as known misses of the 10 ms limit. But, in a few months, we might re-open this package, depending on how frequently the misses are. So you keep all your analysis results and persist what's needed for a later resume'.

The figures are estimates after route C and item 3b's merge, brought up to f3c's review (point 6; f3c-open-shapes-review.md, CORRECTED). None is measured, and no bench builds these shapes.

1. Failed user jobs with .retry deadlines, under one to three prefetch groups.
- Figure: about 500 ms if the origin admits a user request (derived), and that is today's cost too; 9-18 ms otherwise.
  - The derivation: (571.12 − 36.24) ms / 10,000 ≈ 53 µs per heap scan. T20's heap.remove scans the whole heap.
  - The refused form (breaker open): 11.9-22.5 ms after route C and 3b.
  - In production, both paths cost 15-60 ms more, from the originID builds.
- What would close it:
  - A-6 (EngineTimers.swift:111): 11.5-18 ms;
  - an in-place re-admission: 7-12 ms;
  - going lower needs table order, which needs a ruling.
- f3c's route, after OS-1 to OS-3, at stages A / B / C:
  - failedUserRetries: 9.6-19.6 / 8.8-18.8 / 6.0-12.7 ms;
  - failedUserRefused: 8.5-17.8 / 7.7-17.0 / 4.9-10.9 ms;
  - with OS-4 at stage C: 5.2-10.8 ms (its top misses the bar) and 4.1-9.0 ms.
  - f3c's core is 12-18.5 h, on top of route C and 3b.

2. A bulk waiter under three prefetch groups.
- Figure: 12.9-23.3 ms (review must-fix 1, :37; it was 9-17 ms).
- What would close it:
  - an in-place re-queue: 7-11.5 ms;
  - table-order re-queues after an A7-type audit: 4.5-8 ms.
- f3c's route by stage: 7.1-15.3 / 6.3-14.5 / 3.5-8.4 ms. A compaction adds 2-3 ms; OS-5 adds 1.4-2 ms.

3. A prefetch group and a bulk group, under a third group's pending claim.
- Figure: about 21-34 ms (review should-fix 1, :59; it was 10-20 ms).
- Skipping the re-queue breaks R-SYN-3.

items.target: docs/RESIDUAL-RISKS.md, 'Known residual correctness risks (owner ruling 2026-11-06)', and ADR-057: the ENOSPC class
items.source: s3-r28-orchestrator-rulings.md:280-305 (N28, N29), :325 (N31), :336 (N32); .build-orchestrator/s3-rulings-s3f.md:1693 (the owner's answer), :1745-1756 (point 4); docs/adr-drafts/s3f.md:8520-8630; s3f.md table rows correct #1 and #2 (c23 #8)
items.text:
A known residual correctness risk, not blocking, by the owner's rulings:
- N28: 'Agreed let's document it as known risk' (S3-R28 item 1c).
- The close's point 4: 'Yes, the whole class': 'A different answer between the two visit orders, caused by an event inside the disk-full window, is recorded, not fixed. Broken MUSTs, hangs and flaky tests there still block.'

What is exempt: an answer that differs between the two visit orders, caused by an event inside an ENOSPC window (S3-R16 1(a)).

The window runs from a transfer's or a publication's ENOSPC end to the return of spaceFailed's free-space read (item 1c amended, point 6(b)).

The test: N29's T20 test finds the members: 'an answer that differs only because T20 (EngineJobs.swift:360-364) re-queues a job failed at an ENOSPC end in one order and not the other, before that job's space verdict, given at once or at the follow's end after spaceFailed's deferral (EngineFailures.swift:573-582)'.
- Where the test and the owner's words differ, the owner's words decide.
- A late-drain difference is exempt only when its cause falls inside the window. Otherwise point 8 applies, and the orchestrator asks the owner in one line.

Members, measured:
- correct #1 (PROBE-C22C-TS-DRAIN-JOIN, seed 2_029_101):
  - visited first, A, X and V get failed(insufficientSpace(required: 100000, available: 31318659)), with one start;
  - swept first, they get ok(100000 B), with two starts;
  - the control (seed 2_029_201) answers alike in both orders.
- correct #2 (PROBE-C22C-APPLY-IN-READ, seed 2_029_301): visited first, available 31318658 with one start; swept first, ok with two starts.
- Both measured 2/2 on 9aa337c, and again on d88bdb1, 2 rounds each (c23 #8; correct-c22-known-risk-rerun.summary.log).

Members, suspected by code reading only (UNCONFIRMED; each a member only if a run shows the difference):
- W-AWAY;
- W-DB;
- W-JOIN-HOP at a publication's end;
- W-JOIN-HOP in the late drain, under the cause rule;
- item 1's former step-0 shapes;
- f1c-review.md §6's shapes.
A shape a verifier newly finds is included.

Still blocking inside the window: a broken MUST or invariant, a hang or a job that nothing advances, and a flaky test (S3-R16 1(b) to 1(d)), each to the owner. 1(e) and 1(f) there, and every finding after the window, follow point 8.

The user-visible effect (N29): the request was made before the end and replayed in the read. The probes cap retries at 1 (maxAttemptsPerRun = 1, VerifyC22CorrectProbes.swift:258, :387; the default user policy has 2) and script the second attempt to succeed.

Why it is not fixed:
- Four analyses were UNSOUND: f1, f1b, f1c route A and f1c route B.
- Route Q (an independent check of 3-5 h, then 44-67 h; f1c-review.md §3, §9) is not taken.
- Q itself leaves open: W-OBO, W-PEND-LATE's tail, the holder-state approximation (W-BACK-PUB, W-NEST), W-SUPER, lastError's figures, and the out-of-class backlog (W-HOP-DEFERRED, W-PROMO, W-PEND-LATE's non-ENOSPC twin).

No code, test or early probe is added (item 1c's freeze).

Re-open criterion: field frequency.

items.target: docs/RESIDUAL-RISKS.md and ADR-057, 'Point 8: the verification and its findings': c23 #7, the harness's idle predicate
items.text:
Open (point 8; N33). This is a test-harness hang, not an engine hang.

The gap: EngineIntrospection.isIdleSilent ignores an applyAndFollow running in the caller's own task. A test or probe that applies from its own task and drives on isIdleSilent alone can leave an apply pending without noticing.

The evidence, from PROBE-C23C-WALK2:
- 11 of 24 seeds hung past 900 s.
- Stalled seeds 102, 112 and 116 had applyTurnHeld true, applyQueue 29-52, and a store sleeper 0.25 s ahead.
- One 1 s clock advance ended every apply, and all end checks then passed in 8/8 seeds.

ARCHITECTURE §7.8's Idle definition adds the environment census (ManualTimeSource.pendingSleepers == 0), which would have caught these stalls. The harness's settle() checks isIdleSilent alone.

Re-open route: drive until isIdleSilent && appliesInFlight == 0. appliesInFlight is engine state, not in EngineIntrospection.

EngineIntrospection at :37-38 has no appliesInFlight. EngineState.swift:260 `var appliesInFlight = 0`. Tests/ZTronAssetSyncTests/Engine/EngineHarness.swift:271-277 (isQuiet includes pendingSleepers == 0) and :440-443 (settle drives on isIdleSilent). ARCHITECTURE.md:288 (Idle plus the census).

items.target: docs/RESIDUAL-RISKS.md, 'Residual risks (S3-R16; cycle 23)', and ADR-057: RR-24
items.text:
RR-24: a shutdown inside the barrier answers shutDown to every answer that waits for the drain. Non-blocking (S3-R16 item 2; S3-R28 item 2; f2 review must-fix 3).

The difference:
- Visited first, a T20 retry started at a follow's end can serve its joins before a shutdown.
- Swept first, with the follow still owed, the same joins wait behind the verdict, and the shutdown answers them shutDown.

The evidence:
- Probe f2-R1 (visited first, serve forced first): ok(20 B) ×11, 2/2 on 9aa337c; not committed.
- A-T-SD's swept-first arm: shutDown ×11 with 4 joins behind O's verdict, 3/3 in PROBE-C22C-SHUTDOWN-HELD-RETRY. A-T-SD pins it since 03c4e59.

It qualifies EngineFollowBarrierTests.swift:1315 ('Shutdown has no visit-first counterpart'): the answers decided before a shutdown's first turn do have one, and they may differ in this way.
items.code_check: Tests/ZTronAssetSyncTests/Engine/EngineFollowBarrierTests.swift:1315 (the doc text confirmed). EngineFollowBarrierDeferBucketTests.swift:767-775 (A-T-SD, with `holdRetry: true` and the visited-first #require).

items.target: docs/RESIDUAL-RISKS.md, 'Residual risks (S3-R16; cycle 23)', and ADR-057: RR-25, the swept-first backoff
items.text:
RR-25: a purge swept first leaves a failed user job its backoff, where visited first the purge re-admits it. A residual difference under S3-R16 item 2 (f3c §4; its review's 'must add' 6).

The mechanism:
- Swept first, withdrawPurgedJoins takes the groups' joins before they reach the job. The job is never re-laned, so it keeps .failed(.at) and its .retry at its epoch.
- Visited first, the joins are on the job, and the purge's settle re-admits it (T20).

Not probed: T-OS1 (visited first) and T-OS1w (swept first, both drain timings) were not built (f3c §5).

Recorded with N25's row 1.

No spare units (P1):
- The nearest-rank p99 tolerates n − ceil(0.99 n) units over 5 ms: 4 for n < 500, 5 for 500-599 and 6 for n ≥ 600.
- Every run on e840b0e had exactly 5 over: 525, 528, 509 and 519 units.
- The p99 sample is itself a stalled unit, at 4.31-4.89 ms. p95 is about 0.99 ms, and the on-CPU maximum is about 1.0 ms.

Expected failure rate, about 30 % (P2):
- Measurement lens: 17 of 53 recorded runs (Wilson 95 % 0.21-0.45). A Poisson fit at a mean of 4.56 gives P(≥6) = 0.31.
- Refuter: 14 of 50. None of the 9 runs since s3b's reaper-queue change would fail, but 5 of those 9 sit at the limit.
- Some failures came at a quiet load.

At a quiet load, the p99 margin is 2-14 % (4.89, 4.81 and 4.31 ms). The maxima were 10.51, 9.70 and 8.00 ms, so the old maximum assertion would fail.

A P-13 red with no code change falls inside the accepted FAIL (point 3); it is not a new cause. P-13 prints no load averages (P7).

items.target: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §7.10, new paragraph “Follow barrier (F-28)”: base text
items.text: Base, verbatim: “While a follow is owed, nothing is admitted and no space verdict is given: the pump starts, parks and answers nothing; a space sweep waits as an event at its arrival place, runs one follow turn (or one drain turn), and owes a follow-up sweep that judges the jobs still parked once the barrier is down. Every input that is not a real-world ledger input and that decides an answer waits, in arrival order, as an event the drain applies on the state every visit left: a request's join (with its place, its re-check of a parked job and its fail-fast answer); a waiter's withdrawal (the caller is answered at once; the removal and any transfer it stops wait); a conditions element's pass; an origin's re-admission; a backoff's end; a throttle's answer turn; a space sweep's verdicts; and every exit of an attempt while the barrier holds (a final answer, a retry, a count toward the caps, an ENOSPC, the offline exit, a 429's park, a pause's park or re-queue, a re-queue), each with its fail-fast answers. Applied on arrival, because they decide no answer and differ from a visit-first engine only in order: a group's release and its later turns, a purge's withdrawals, a claim's end, a run's and a re-attachment's removals, a publication's commit (its unbound ids follow their content through joins that wait), a superseded publication and a cancelled attempt's ENOENT re-queue. Each waiting event reads the world as it stood at its arrival, and a follow's visit reads it as it stood at the apply: while the barrier holds, the origin's throttle and circuit breaker, the conditions and the thermal pause, and the network edge are kept as views, one per change, and a decision taken in a replay or a visit reads its own view. A place given there is refused by its view's throttle or breaker, and every start reads the live throttle, breaker, slots and space, so no request goes to an origin whose throttle or open breaker is live (R-SYN-5). A 429 throttles its origin on arrival, for the backoff of the lane the owed visits leave the job (its interests whose ids the engine's copy still maps to it), else of the job's own lane, unless its `Retry-After` exceeds `maxRetryAfter`; its park and answers wait. The follow's own visit moves the ids it moves, in its order, and a waiting verdict is then given to the ids left. The follow's last turn pumps and then applies the events, at most 512 per turn; no pump runs during or between those turns, the last one checks the run and pumps, and no run settles before it. A second apply keeps the visits still owed in their order; the jobs it finds unfollowed but not owed are visited after the older passes end. Outside the class (R1): a free-space read and the bytes an ended transfer frees apply when they arrive and are read live (L4-R7). The barrier guarantees the answers, the MUSTs and the invariants of a visit-first engine, not its order: the differences in order, place, timing and backoff length are the residual risks RR-1 to RR-6 of the WP-F draft (Stage 3 close-out cycles 9 to 13, S3-R11, S3-R14 to S3-R16; design D3).” Apply cycles 14-22's edits to it (next four items). Do not write cycle 3's `pumpWaitsForFollow` dispatch sentence or any other superseded text.

items.text: The visit sentence, final form: cycle 16's text replaces cycle 15's, and cycle 17 inserts after “…the ids the applies followed since its deferral moved”: “A visit compares its apply with the job's attempt end and exit verdict, counted in applies followed, and meets the job as a visit-first engine's visit met it at that apply. A visit that meets a job publishing, failed in its publication's bookkeeping with no verdict yet for an apply made while it published, or failed with its verdict waiting keeps the job's bytes and publication. It re-routes at once the moved ids a visit-first engine had moved before the publication began or the verdict arrived (the visit spends that set, and so does the end of its follow). It passes the others, which the publication's outcome or the verdict answers. After the verdict, the drain moves from the job the verdict leaves the ids the applies followed since its deferral moved. Before the verdict, the drain takes off the job the ids a visit-first engine's visits had moved off it before the verdict arrived and that are still on it (a later apply moved them back), and re-routes them after the verdict; a publication that ended with no apply since keeps only the ids the copy lists elsewhere. A visit's join onto a job whose verdict waits waits behind that verdict.” Next comes the attempt's-end text (cycles 18-20 item). Cycle 16's “(S3-R18, S3-R18a, S3-R19)” goes at the end of the inserted run. The 429 sentence: after cycle 15's parenthetical, add cycle 16's “and, of another job whose verdict waits with an apply followed since, the interests the drain moves onto it after the verdict, less those the verdict answers”. Cycle 17 changes “less those the verdict answers” to “less those the verdict's replay answers on the job it meets (a `Retry-After` beyond the kept lane's cap, a park's fail-fast and an ENOSPC's verdict included)”, and adds “the interests the drain takes off a waiting verdict's job and re-routes onto it”. items.text: Replace cycle 17's attempt's-end sentence with this final form (cycle 18, edited by cycles 19 and 20): “An attempt's end (its publication's start, or its exit verdict's deferral), and each apply made while a follow is owed for every job whose publication runs (under the outgoing copy, before it is replaced), record the moves of the interests other jobs hold in ids the copy maps to the job's content and whose owed visits would move them. The attempt's end makes the first 64, within half a turn's ids; the follow's turns make the rest, before any visit and within 256 holders and 512 ids a turn, each under the copy that found it, a move of more ids than the turn has left going on in the next; a move onto a job whose attempt has since ended is dropped, and the holder's visit moves the ids. While a move is owed the follow is owed. A visit, the drain's visit after a verdict included, moves at most a turn's 512 ids. Its rest goes on first in the follow's next turns once no move is owed, and the follow stays owed until its last id moved; the events after the drain's visit wait for it. The drain's visits after verdicts share the ids its turn has left (the follow's last turn's, or a whole turn's in a drain turn of its own); once they are spent, the rest of the batch waits, in order, for the next drain turn. A visit that moves every id off a job that is not publishing supersedes the job in its first turn; a publication binds its ids only once no move onto or off its job, and no rest of a visit of its job, is owed.” Cycle 19 inserts its sentences between “the follow is owed” and “, and a publication binds”; the punctuation at the joins is the writer's. items.source: Gap, not in the draft. Cycle 21's owed-answers text (s3f.md:9820-9824) contradicts the current wording.
items.text: ARCH:307 says the engine's shutdown returns “only after every owned task is cancelled and joined and every continuation resumed with `.shutDown`”. Since cycle 21, owed answers are resumed with their stored values, not `.shutDown`: these are the answers that a resolution of more than `answersPerTurn` interests had already computed. Since S3F-4 the order is: cancel owned tasks, cancel running handles, drain and settle in slices, join each task and drain again after each join, invalidate, then `closeStore()`. Amend to “…every continuation resumed (with `.shutDown`, except owed answers, which keep their computed values)”, and state the order.

items.text: Context: the six purge misses are known misses; the owner needs a field signal. Options S1 to S4 come from `end-sooner-options.md` §4. Decision: S1, one `.info` line on `.sync`, “long purge turn: <ms> ms, <jobs> jobs, <groups> groups”, above `SyncEngine.turnTimeLimit` (10 ms). It names no id, hash, URL, path or key. It changes no public API, adds nothing on the main thread, and uses the injected clock (C4). Consequences: the text, category, level and threshold are a soft contract, and an app reads the line through its `LogSink` or `OSLogStore` as the purge misses' re-open criterion. Whether `OSLogStore` keeps `.info` lines is UNVERIFIED (C7). Not NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW unless S2 to S4 are chosen later.

items.target: Orchestrator decision: RR-20's proposed fix
items.text: RR-20: when the owed move takes a job's only id, the publication binds nothing yet books a commit and an object success. Its staged `.part` stays until staging GC (R-CLN-3), and the free-space estimate drops by its bytes until the next read. Both orders give the same answers (W gets `integrityFailure`; VERIFY-C18R-EMPTY-BINDING 2/2). The finding proposes discarding the staged file and retiring the job without a commit. That changes publication bookkeeping, so it is left for the orchestrator and Stage 5.

items.target: docs/RESIDUAL-RISKS.md (Stage 5): RR-21's residuals
items.source: s3f.md:6988-7001; rulings S3-R24 item 5 (timing class), S3-R26 item 1 (rulings 1-5), S3-R27 item 12.2
items.text: Each residual is a timing class only while the event lands between the two engines' answers. (1) A cancel or a release between the owing instant and a T21 or present pair's replay gives `.cancelled` (ruling 1). (2) The global hold delays unrelated publications, and an apply during it can drop a held job's ids (ruling 2). (3) A pin whose job committed, was superseded or was ENOENT-re-queued before the replay, narrowed by `PinEnd` (e1-R1 `5ad245d`, e1-PS `b4eebb1`): commit or supersede gives the copy in force then; ENOENT gives the copy until the first adopted after the re-queue; a job with no record follows the copy at the replay (ruling 3). (4) A purge's dropped bindings, an eviction or a quarantine in the window turns a present answer into a join (ruling 5). (5) A heal of a T21 system item's asset in the window is forgotten (ruling 1's class; PROBE-RR21-HEAL-T21 breaks nothing). (6) The broad idle guards keep every binding and the watcher while any event waits. (7) Admissions and run settlement wait for every owed batch, about 20 drain turns at 10,000 ids. (8) Each owed batch keeps its copy and layers alive (memory only). Item B's residuals, with class, condition and test, are under the draft's cycle 21, “Step 4”.

items.target: docs/RESIDUAL-RISKS.md: the ENOSPC class, a known residual correctness risk
items.source: s3f.md:8520-8631; owner rulings N28 (S3-R28 item 1c) and N31 (close ruling point 4)
items.text: An answer that differs between the two visit orders, caused by an event inside an ENOSPC window, is recorded, not fixed. The window runs from a transfer's or publication's ENOSPC end to the return of `spaceFailed`'s read. Correct #1 (PROBE-C22C-TS-DRAIN-JOIN, seed 2_029_101): visited first, A, X and V get `failed(insufficientSpace(required: 100000, available: 31318659))` with one start; swept first they get `ok(100000 B)` with two starts. The control, seed 2_029_201, gives `ok` and two starts in both orders. Correct #2 (PROBE-C22C-APPLY-IN-READ, seed 2_029_301) diverges the same way for A and X. Both still reproduce on `d88bdb1` (c23 #8). The probes cap `maxAttemptsPerRun = 1` (the default is 2) and script the second attempt to succeed. The route that would close it is route Q, at 44-67 h plus a 3-5 h check; the analyses were found UNSOUND four times. Frozen: `metInItsAttempt`, `relane`'s guard, `Job.transferSpaceEnd`, `AttemptEnd.stamped`. Still blocking inside the window: a broken MUST or invariant, a hang, and a flaky test.

issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/SyncEngine.swift:13-18; the description of this edit at docs/DECISIONS.md:690 ("the three paths that resume a continuation after it leaves its table")
issues.problem: The rewritten invariant says every continuation "is resumed exactly once, after it leaves its table through `removeValue`". It then names the follow-barrier withdrawal as one of the "Three paths [that] resume it later than it leaves". The merged code does the opposite. `withdraw` (EngineCommands.swift:176-186) resumes the waiter's continuation first (:178). Off the barrier it then sets `self.state.waiters[token] = nil` in the same turn (:184), which is an assignment, not `removeValue`. Behind the barrier it sets only `continuation = nil` (:180) and defers `.removal(token, …)` to the drain (:181). The record stays in `waiters` until `replayRemoval` removes it (EngineFollow.swift:1024-1031: `if let waiter = self.state.waiters[token], waiter.continuation == nil { self.state.waiters[token] = nil …`). So on the barrier path the caller is resumed turns BEFORE its record leaves the table. Shutdown also takes the table out by whole assignment (EngineShutdown.swift:61-62), not by `removeValue`. The base text (8d86acb: "resumed only through `removeValue` on its table") was stale, and the replacement is still false of the merged code. DECISIONS.md:690 states the same inverted framing; it is recorded honestly as not independently verified.
issues.fix: Reword lines 13-18 to match the code. Suggested text: "Every continuation (waiters, groups, runs, `start`/`sync` joiners, `waitUntil`) is resumed exactly once and leaves its table in the same turn (through `removeValue` or a nil assignment, or with the whole table at shutdown), and every table is settled at registration, on each transition, on withdrawal, on purge and on shutdown (sync-1 S1-02). Two paths resume a continuation in a later turn than the one it leaves in (Stage 3): shutdown's bounded slices, and the answer follow-ups (`owedAnswers`) for a resolution of more than `answersPerTurn` interests. Behind the follow barrier the order is reversed: a withdrawing caller is resumed at once, and its record stays in `waiters` without its continuation until the drain removes it with its interest (`replayRemoval`)." Change DECISIONS.md:690's parenthetical to match, e.g. "(the two paths that resume a continuation after it leaves its table, and the barrier withdrawal that resumes it before)".
